medium.title: Generic API Key shipped in the app
medium.description: A Generic API Key appears in app_modules/503_PREMIUM_API_KEY.js at line 8. Anything inside the package is readable by anyone who downloads it, so this value is public. The app contains a hardcoded API key 'sk_live_dvrn_9f8a2c1b4e7d' used to authenticate requests to the premium content endpoint (/api/premium). Since the key is shipped in the clear within the JavaScript bundle, any user can extract it and access premium services directly.
medium.impact: Whatever the credential unlocks is reachable by anyone who extracts it from the APK.
medium.recommendation: Move the secret server-side, or restrict the key by package signature and API scope and rotate the exposed value.

medium.title: Sensitive value 'authToken' stored with setItem in unencrypted storage
medium.description: The app writes a value under the key 'authToken' with setItem, the AsyncStorage API. AsyncStorage keeps values as plain text in the app's data directory. The app stores the 'authToken' in AsyncStorage, which is an unencrypted key-value store. On rooted devices or via backup extraction, an attacker can retrieve this session token in plain text.
medium.impact: Anyone with a backup of the app data, root on the device, or a debuggable build reads the value directly.

medium.description: The DebugModule exposes a native method 'readInternalFile' to the React Native bridge that reads any file from the filesystem based on a user-supplied path without validation. info.title: No screenshot protection: FLAG_SECURE is never set
info.description: Nothing in the app sets WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE, so every screen can be screenshotted or recorded and appears in the recent-apps snapshot.
info.impact: Credentials, balances or personal data on screen end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview.
info.recommendation: Set FLAG_SECURE on the windows of screens that show credentials or account data.

reasons: Screen contents not protected from capture. Without FLAG_SECURE, what a screen shows can end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview. That matters on screens showing credentials, card numbers or balances; on its own it is a hardening note.

info.title: Plain HTTP endpoint in app_modules/494_API_BASE_URL.js
info.description: The app is configured to use a plain HTTP endpoint (http://10.0.2.2:3000). Sensitive data, including user credentials during login (app_modules/493_login.js) and the session authToken, are transmitted in cleartext, making them susceptible to interception via Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks.

reasons: Cleartext traffic reaches at most CVSS 7.5 (High); the vector given scores this finding above anything the class does.
The plain-HTTP address in the code is a development host (private or loopback network), not an endpoint reached over the internet.
The IP address 10.0.2.2 is an emulator-only loopback and is not reachable on real devices, indicating this is a debug configuration.

info.description: A private (RFC 1918) address appears in app_modules/494_API_BASE_URL.js at line 8. It names a development or internal host and grants nothing by itself; it is recorded because it tells a reader about internal infrastructure, or that a development endpoint shipped in the build.
info.impact: None directly. If the app sends requests to it, the cleartext and endpoint findings for that host carry the risk.
info.recommendation: Point release builds at production hosts through build configuration, and leave development addresses out of them.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 24 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "com.dvrn.app". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task.
info.impact: On a device running Android 10 or lower, a malicious app can put a look-alike screen on top of this app's task, phishing credentials or keeping the real app from being shown.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.
